result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with row houses and mature trees. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the environment lacks formal crossing infrastructure and is dominated by on-street parking that creates visual obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly shorter individuals like children, who may attempt to cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible street segment.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crossings in a residential area may lead to unpredictable pedestrian movements across the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by allowing pedestrians to see past parked cars before entering the travel lane.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark pedestrian crossings with high-visibility paint to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to ensure vehicle speeds remain low in this residential context.

result.summary: The image depicts a typical urban residential street characterized by row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While the environment is low-speed and residential, it lacks formal pedestrian safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, traffic calming, or dedicated lighting for the walkway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street creates significant sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross and for drivers to see them.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Clutter
hazards.description: Trash bins and other residential items are placed on the narrow sidewalk, reducing the effective walking width.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersections to improve visibility (daylighting) and shorten the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks at the nearest intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to ensure vehicle speeds remain consistently low in this residential area.

result.summary: The image shows a dense residential street with row houses and a continuous, well-maintained sidewalk. While the pedestrian environment is clear of obstructions, there is no physical buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and parked vehicles significantly limit visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the road, increasing risk for mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no buffer zone, trees, or furniture to protect pedestrians from moving traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire curb line visible in the image.
